- Wikipedia: Information about: Cromoglicic acid
Section: Introduction
Cromoglicic acid (INN)—also referred to as cromolyn (USAN), cromoglycate (former BAN), or cromoglicate—is traditionally described as a mast cell stabilizer, and is commonly marketed as the sodium salt sodium cromoglicate or cromolyn sodium.  This drug prevents the release of inflammatory chemicals such as histamine from mast cells. It is considered a breakthrough drug in management of asthma, as the patients can be freed from steroids in many cases; however, it is mainly effective as a prophylaxis for allergic and exercise-induced asthma, not as a treatment for acute asthma attacks.[citation needed]
Section: History
Cromolyn was discovered in 1965 by Roger Altounyan, a pharmacologist who had asthma. Altounyan was investigating certain plants and herbs which have bronchodilating properties. One such plant was khella (Ammi visnaga) which had been used as a muscle relaxant since ancient times in Egypt. Altounyan deliberately inhaled derivatives of the active ingredient khellin to determine if they could block his asthma attacks. After several years of trial, he isolated an effective and safe asthma-preventing compound called cromolyn sodium.[2]
Section: Preparations
as a nasal spray (Rynacrom (UK), Lomusol (France), Nasalcrom (the only over-the-counter form, US), Prevalin (non-direct version, NL)) to treat allergic rhinitis. in a nebulizer solution for aerosol administration to treat asthma. as an inhaler (Intal, Fisons Pharmaceuticals, UK) for preventive management of asthma.[3] The maker of Intal, King Pharmaceuticals, has discontinued manufacturing the inhaled form, cromolyn sodium inhalation aerosol, due to issues involving CFC-free propellant.[4]  As stocks are depleted, this inhaler preparation will no longer be available to patients.[5] In the EU it is manufactured without CFCs by Sanofi, although it must be imported from Canada or Mexico for USA residents. as eye drops (Opticrom and Optrex Allergy (UK), Crolom, Cromolyn (Canada)) for allergic conjunctivitis[6] in an oral form (Gastrocrom, Nalcrom) to treat mastocytosis,[7] mast cell activation syndrome, dermatographic urticaria and ulcerative colitis. Another oral product, Intercron (sodium cromoglicate in distilled water, from Zambon France), is used for food allergies.
Section: Mechanism of action
"Cromolyn works because it prevents the release of mediators that would normally attract inflammatory cells and because it stabilizes the inflammatory cells. MCT mast cells found in the mucosa are stabilised."[8] Nedocromil is another mast cell stabilizer that also works in controlling asthma.
The underlying mechanism of action is not fully understood; for while cromoglicate stabilizes mast cells, this mechanism is probably not why it works in asthma.[9]  Pharmaceutical companies have produced 20 related compounds that are equally or more potent at stabilising mast cells and none of them have shown any anti-asthmatic effect.[9] It is more likely that these work by inhibiting the response of sensory C fibers to the irritant capsaicin, inhibiting local axon reflexes involved in asthma, and may inhibit the release of preformed T cell cytokines and mediators involved in asthma.[10] It is known to somewhat inhibit chloride channels (37% ± 7%)[11] and thus may inhibit the: exaggerated neuronal reflexes triggered by stimulation of irritant receptors on sensory nerve endings (e.g. exercise-induced asthma) release of preformed cytokines from several type of inflammatory cells (T cells, eosinophils) in allergen-induced asthma

Obat ini mencegah pelepasan zat kimia inflamasi seperti histamin dari sel mast. Asam kromoglikat telah menjadi pengobatan non-kortikosteroid pilihan dalam pengobatan asma, yang sebagian besar telah digantikan oleh antagonis reseptor leukotriena karena keamanan dan kenyamanannya. Asam kromoglikat memerlukan pemberian empat kali sehari, dan tidak memberikan manfaat tambahan dalam kombinasi dengan kortikosteroid hirup.[1]
Section: Sejarah
Kromolin ditemukan pada tahun 1965 oleh Roger Altounyan, seorang farmakolog yang menderita asma. Altounyan sedang menyelidiki tanaman dan herba tertentu yang memiliki sifat bronkodilatasi. Salah satu tanaman tersebut adalah khella (Ammi visnaga) yang telah digunakan sebagai pelemas otot sejak zaman kuno di Mesir. Altounyan sengaja menghirup turunan bahan aktif khellin untuk menentukan apakah mereka dapat memblokir serangan asmanya. Setelah beberapa tahun percobaan, ia mengisolasi senyawa pencegah asma yang efektif dan aman yang disebut natrium kromolin.[2]
Section: Preparasi
sebagai semprotan hidung untuk mengobati rinitis alergi. dalam larutan nebulizer untuk pemberian aerosol untuk mengobati asma. sebagai inhaler untuk manajemen pencegahan asma.[3] King Pharmaceuticals telah menghentikan produksi bentuk inhalasi, aerosol inhalasi kromolin natrium, karena masalah yang melibatkan propelan bebas CFC.[4] Karena stok menipis, sediaan inhaler ini tidak akan tersedia lagi bagi pasien.[5] Di Uni Eropa, obat ini diproduksi tanpa CFC oleh Sanofi, meskipun harus diimpor dari Kanada atau Meksiko untuk penduduk AS. sebagai obat tetes mata untuk konjungtivitis alergi[6] dalam bentuk oral (Gastrocrom, Nalcrom) untuk mengobati mastositosis,[7] sindrom aktivasi sel mast, urtikaria dermatografik, dan kolitis ulseratif. Produk oral lainnya yakni Intercron (natrium kromoglikat dalam air suling, dari Zambon Prancis), digunakan untuk alergi makanan.
Section: Mekanisme kerja
"Kromolin bekerja karena mencegah pelepasan mediator yang biasanya menarik sel inflamasi dan karena menstabilkan sel inflamasi. Sel mast MCT yang ditemukan di mukosa distabilkan."[8] Nedokromil adalah penstabil sel mast lain yang juga bekerja dalam mengendalikan asma. Mekanisme kerja yang mendasarinya belum sepenuhnya dipahami; karena meskipun kromoglikat menstabilkan sel mast, mekanisme ini mungkin bukan alasan mengapa ia bekerja pada asma. Perusahaan farmasi telah memproduksi 20 senyawa terkait yang sama atau lebih kuat dalam menstabilkan sel mast dan tidak satu pun dari senyawa tersebut menunjukkan efek anti-asma.[9] Kemungkinan besar senyawa ini bekerja dengan menghambat respons serabut C sensorik terhadap iritan kapsaisin, menghambat refleks akson lokal yang terlibat dalam asma, dan dapat menghambat pelepasan sitokin dan mediator sel T yang telah terbentuk sebelumnya yang terlibat dalam asma.[10] Diketahui bahwa zat ini agak menghambat saluran klorida (37% ± 7%)[11] dan dengan demikian dapat menghambat: refleks neuronal berlebihan yang dipicu oleh stimulasi reseptor iritan pada ujung saraf sensorik (misalnya asma akibat olahraga) pelepasan sitokin yang telah terbentuk sebelumnya dari beberapa jenis sel inflamasi (sel T, eosinofil) pada asma akibat alergen

Section: Introduction
Cromoglicic acid (INN)—also referred to as cromolyn (USAN), cromoglycate (former BAN), or cromoglicate—is traditionally described as a mast cell stabilizer, and is commonly marketed as the sodium salt sodium cromoglicate or cromolyn sodium.  This drug prevents the release of inflammatory chemicals such as histamine from mast cells. It is considered a breakthrough drug in management of asthma, as the patients can be freed from steroids in many cases; however, it is mainly effective as a prophylaxis for allergic and exercise-induced asthma, not as a treatment for acute asthma attacks.[citation needed]
Section: History
Cromolyn was discovered in 1965 by Roger Altounyan, a pharmacologist who had asthma. Altounyan was investigating certain plants and herbs which have bronchodilating properties. One such plant was khella (Ammi visnaga) which had been used as a muscle relaxant since ancient times in Egypt. Altounyan deliberately inhaled derivatives of the active ingredient khellin to determine if they could block his asthma attacks. After several years of trial, he isolated an effective and safe asthma-preventing compound called cromolyn sodium.[2]
Section: Preparations
as a nasal spray (Rynacrom (UK), Lomusol (France), Nasalcrom (the only over-the-counter form, US), Prevalin (non-direct version, NL)) to treat allergic rhinitis. in a nebulizer solution for aerosol administration to treat asthma. as an inhaler (Intal, Fisons Pharmaceuticals, UK) for preventive management of asthma.[3] The maker of Intal, King Pharmaceuticals, has discontinued manufacturing the inhaled form, cromolyn sodium inhalation aerosol, due to issues involving CFC-free propellant.[4]  As stocks are depleted, this inhaler preparation will no longer be available to patients.[5] In the EU it is manufactured without CFCs by Sanofi, although it must be imported from Canada or Mexico for USA residents. as eye drops (Opticrom and Optrex Allergy (UK), Crolom, Cromolyn (Canada)) for allergic conjunctivitis[6] in an oral form (Gastrocrom, Nalcrom) to treat mastocytosis,[7] mast cell activation syndrome, dermatographic urticaria and ulcerative colitis. Another oral product, Intercron (sodium cromoglicate in distilled water, from Zambon France), is used for food allergies.
Section: Mechanism of action
"Cromolyn works because it prevents the release of mediators that would normally attract inflammatory cells and because it stabilizes the inflammatory cells. MCT mast cells found in the mucosa are stabilised."[8] Nedocromil is another mast cell stabilizer that also works in controlling asthma.
The underlying mechanism of action is not fully understood; for while cromoglicate stabilizes mast cells, this mechanism is probably not why it works in asthma.[9]  Pharmaceutical companies have produced 20 related compounds that are equally or more potent at stabilising mast cells and none of them have shown any anti-asthmatic effect.[9] It is more likely that these work by inhibiting the response of sensory C fibers to the irritant capsaicin, inhibiting local axon reflexes involved in asthma, and may inhibit the release of preformed T cell cytokines and mediators involved in asthma.[10] It is known to somewhat inhibit chloride channels (37% ± 7%)[11] and thus may inhibit the: exaggerated neuronal reflexes triggered by stimulation of irritant receptors on sensory nerve endings (e.g. exercise-induced asthma) release of preformed cytokines from several type of inflammatory cells (T cells, eosinophils) in allergen-induced asthma
